title: Closure profile — v1.0
description: plan.md §4's worked example, chainlink #25. One per cluster at specs/_closure/<cluster>.json (workspace-level, like specs/_conflicts/ -- a cluster spans crates by construction). A closure profile is a PER-CLUSTER declared property with a kind; there is deliberately no artifact in this pipeline that asserts closure globally (plan.md §4: 'Never a global pipeline guarantee'), and scripts/gate_g14.py prints per-cluster outcomes only. Two clusters with identical condition bits carry different guarantees, which is what closure_kind exists to keep visible: a Kani-owned cluster is `bounded` and must never read as full closure. Every condition scripts/gate_g14.py can recompute is recomputed and rejected on disagreement in BOTH directions (the same discipline G1b applies to computed eligibility in I) -- a declared condition bit is a claim to check, never an input to trust. The one exception is generic_callees_type_universal_or_creusot_owned (CG3), which needs type information no artifact in this pipeline carries; it stays a human declaration and the gate says so rather than silently treating it as verified. A cluster that cannot meet its conditions carries a degradation record instead (docs/degradation-record-schema.json), which is a declared state, not a failure.

cluster.description: Must equal the filename stem exactly (G1b, scripts/validate_closure.py), the same discipline boundary_id/interaction_id/bridge_id/report_id already follow.

closure_kind.description: plan.md §4's table: Creusot/Verus-owned -> deductive (universal over inputs, modulo SMT completeness and trusted specs); Kani-owned -> bounded (holds only within unwind/harness bounds and enumerated monomorphizations). Recomputed from the evidence kinds actually present across the transitive closure; a profile claiming `deductive` over a closure containing a Kani result is a G17 hard error, not a rounding-up.

work_packages.description: The work-package manifests whose definition_of_done makes up this cluster (ci/manifest/<id>.json). An addition to plan.md §4's worked example, which names a cluster without saying what is in it: G14's transitive closure has to start somewhere, and deriving cluster membership by guesswork is exactly the kind of implicit scoping the rest of this pipeline refuses. The closure itself is NOT limited to these -- a required guarantee provided by a work package outside the cluster is followed and checked like any other, which is the whole point of a transitive closure.

conditions.description: plan.md §4's condition block, field for field. Every one of these must hold for the cluster to close; a degradation record names the ones that do not (docs/degradation-record-schema.json's failed_conditions, whose enum is exactly these keys).

single_verifier_system.description: One verifier system across the whole closure. False is the CG1 case (cross-verifier composition has no soundness theorem) and needs a degradation record with the `harness-tested` ceiling. Recomputed from the evidence kinds in the closure.

owning_verifier.description: The verifier system this cluster's closure is owned by. Recomputed from the closure's achieved records; disagreement is rejected.

protocol_class_all_pairwise.description: Every bridge in the closure is protocol_class: pairwise (docs/bridge-schema.json). A non-pairwise protocol needs its own artifact or debt record (G15) and cannot be closed over by a pairwise bridge argument. Recomputed.

unresolved_indirect_calls_at_or_above_me.description: plan.md §4's own condition name. Read from scripts/gate_r1_g16.py's unresolved_at_or_above_medium() over the C_static reports (chainlink #24) -- never recomputed here, so the closure profile and the R1/G16 gate can never disagree about what 'unresolved' means. Must be 0 for the cluster to close.

generic_callees_type_universal_or_creuso.description: CG3: Kani verifies generics per monomorphization, so universality over type parameters does not hold there. THE ONE CONDITION THE GATE CANNOT RECOMPUTE -- no artifact in this pipeline carries the type information it would need. It stays a human declaration, and scripts/gate_g14.py reports it as declared-not-verified every time rather than letting it pass as checked.

transitive_assumptions_within_policy.description: Every assumption appearing in ANY achieved record anywhere in the transitive closure is allowed by the cluster's own entry requirements' trust_policy -- not merely by the policy of the edge it sits on. plan.md §8.5's opening case: 'Direct A->B checking passes while a C-level assumption sits below policy.' Recomputed.

scc_wellfoundedness_discharged.description: CG6. `not-applicable` is required when the closure is acyclic -- a profile claiming `true` there would be claiming a discharge it never needed, which is a vacuous truth this schema declines to accept (the same objection #48 raised against a vacuous OK). When the closure has a cycle, this must be `true` AND every non-trivial SCC must have a matching entry in scc_discharges.

scc_discharges.description: plan.md §8.5's CG6 requirement: 'mutual satisfaction is not soundness'. One entry per non-trivial strongly-connected component in the closure. Required by G14 whenever a cycle exists (not by this schema, which cannot see the graph); an entry naming an SCC that does not exist is rejected as stale, so a discharge can never be a leftover asserting something about a graph that has since changed.

members.description: The obligations in this SCC, exactly -- matched as a set against the SCC the gate computes. minItems 2 because a self-dependency (an obligation whose provider requires it back) is reported by G14 as its own single-member cycle and discharged by naming it twice would be nonsense; a genuine self-loop is a modelling error to fix, not to discharge.

kind.description: plan.md §8.5's three named forms of well-foundedness argument. The vocabulary is closed deliberately: a free-text kind would let 'we reviewed it and it's fine' pass as a discharge.

argument.description: The actual argument: what the step index / measure / stratification is, and why no instantaneous circular dependence remains. Prose, human-authored, human-reviewed -- the gate checks that it exists, covers the right SCC, and was reviewed; it cannot check that it is correct, and does not claim to.

obligation_id.description: <Concept>.<id>, the same shape as a boundary contract's callee_guarantees entries and a work-package manifest's own obligation_id.

review.description: plan.md §7.2 lists closure-profile/degradation-record acceptance as a human checkpoint. Attached by review_checkpoint.approve(), never authored by a proposing model.
